sandbox.reason: turned off by the owner (scoutctl sandbox off)

gate_probe.reason: claude ran, but Scout's kb-read-gate never fired

problems.summary: 1 scheduled run in the last 7 days changed a protected file (a runner script, agent settings or Scout's schedule) in git. Scout put it back in a new commit.
problems.fix: Read that run's log (the `integrity check:` lines name the files and the restoring commit) and its session, to see what made it change them.

problems.summary: Scheduled runs are paused: the Claude Code they use didn't load Scout's privacy checks (claude ran, but Scout's kb-read-gate never fired).
problems.fix: Check again after updating Scout or Claude Code. Runs resume on their own once the check passes.

problems.summary: You turned write protection off, so scheduled runs could change the files that decide which of Scout's checks run. Scout's privacy checks still run.
problems.fix: Turn it back on unless you are fixing something that needs it off.

problems.summary: The last scheduled run ran without its commit and Telegram broker, so it could still write the vault's git history directly and read the Telegram token (git-safe-commit.sh predates the broker).
problems.fix: If the reason names an old git-safe-commit.sh, update Scout. Otherwise the run log's `broker:` lines say why; the next run tries again on its own.
